findings.detail: All common logical actions have equal counts; Native alone has pollTaskRuns twice and desktop.session once. Phase-level aggregates cannot determine per-read WS/HTTP ordering.

DesktopIntegration reads the owner-wide task list for badge and completion notifications even without local enrollment. Initial result seeds notification history without replaying existing terminal runs.

UNRESOLVED creates no real ticket; first result supplies validated personal home. onopen creates a fresh catch-up obligation. A read begun before that boundary cannot prove coverage; already-ready same-kind coverage and committed exact-cache proof are already reusable.
Task list chooses latest run per issue for up to 200 issues, while thread list chooses up to 200 runs and has different fields. It cannot substitute without loss.
cacheWorkspace is a selected membership with id and role. Safe session contains user and session id only. Vault workspace is a selected workspace cookie, not a fresh personal-home assertion.

Existing successful /api/workspace response has live.homeWorkspaceId from ownerLiveScope. This value arrives in a parallel read and is distinct from selected workspace; using it cannot certify coverage of an earlier task read by itself.
Native BundledLive asks only for revisions and bridge send accepts ping only. Presence acknowledgement barrier cannot be assumed as the cause of this Native startup.

Current SWR read start is before hydration and posted-task batching. A request actually dispatched after an obligation may still be conservatively revalidated. No per-invocation evidence proves that schedule in this run; any refinement requires exact per-read identity and real dispatch proof, retaining SWR commit/revision/error/owner fences.

suggestedRegressions: Real SWR first poll -> owner-home reply -> a server write before socket opens -> open/ready must still produce a second read and latest badge.
Already-ready same-owner home channel + read begun after coverage + exact committed cache object + late task subscriber should remain one read under existing proof.
Candidate only: fetcher is queued before Live obligation but its actual native HTTP dispatch is after; exact dispatch proof may permit one read, while a pre-obligation send must still reread.
Retain higher/unversioned push, discarded or comparator-retained result, callback failure, hidden view and owner/cache/connection retirement regressions.
